summary: On node1, /srv/data is now a dedicated XFS filesystem (loop-mounted from /var/lib/srv-data-fs/srvdata.img via /etc/fstab with the uquota option) owned by datauser, with an XFS user quota of 100MB soft/hard set via xfs_quota. Enforcement is filesystem-native (kernel EDQUOT, not a wrapper script) and was verified both before and after a full node reboot, confirming the mount/quota configuration persists via fstab and continues enforcing the 100MB cap post-restart.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: root fs is XFS mounted noquota with no spare block device, so created a dedicated loop-backed 2G XFS image for /srv/data instead of altering root fs mount options
Created /var/lib/srv-data-fs/srvdata.img, formatted as XFS, added fstab entry '/var/lib/srv-data-fs/srvdata.img /srv/data xfs loop,uquota 0 0', mounted it
chowned /srv/data to datauser and set xfs_quota limit bsoft=100m bhard=100m for datauser
Verified enforcement pre-reboot: writes up to 100MB succeed, next write fails with 'Disk quota exceeded' at exactly the 100MB boundary; cleaned up test files
Captured baseline boot_id and quota state on node1, issued a background 'systemctl reboot' whose acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until exec was available again; confirmed boot_id changed and fresh uptime, proving an actual restart occurred
Post-reboot verified /srv/data mount, ownership, and xfs_quota state/report persisted automatically via fstab
Re-ran a 150MB write test live post-reboot to confirm the kernel still enforces the 100MB cap after restart; cleaned up test file, leaving /srv/data empty with quota at 0 used / 100M limit

evidence.summary: useradd -m datauser succeeded; id shows uid=1000(datauser)

evidence.requirement: /srv/data set up as a filesystem-enforced quota target (dedicated XFS mount with usrquota)
evidence.summary: Created and formatted XFS loop image, added fstab entry with uquota option, mounted at /srv/data; mount output shows 'type xfs (...,usrquota)'

evidence.requirement: 100MB quota limit applied to datauser on /srv/data
evidence.summary: xfs_quota limit set bsoft=100m bhard=100m for datauser; report confirms 100M/100M soft/hard for datauser

evidence.requirement: Quota is enforced by the filesystem itself (kernel-level EDQUOT), not merely configured
evidence.summary: datauser dd write of 80MB succeeded, second 80MB write failed mid-stream with 'Disk quota exceeded' at the 100MB boundary; xfs_quota report shows Used=100M

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline: boot identity and quota-enforcing mount state captured
evidence.summary: Test files cleaned (quota back to 0 used); boot_id 434803ac-a01f-4272-ba59-a0cdb0c4dd92 captured; mount and 'xfs_quota state -u' both show usrquota Accounting/Enforcement ON
Backgrounded 'systemctl reboot' via nohup/disown returned 'reboot scheduled' before the node dropped

evidence.requirement: Node actually restarted (changed boot identity), not just time elapsed
evidence.summary: Connection timed out/reset during reboot window, then exec succeeded again with new boot_id afd84d52-7891-42f8-94ad-0c3dd704c4ef (differs from baseline) and uptime '0 min', proving a real reboot

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: quota-enforced mount, ownership, and limits persisted and are still live
evidence.summary: After reboot, /srv/data still mounted xfs with usrquota, owned by datauser:datauser, and xfs_quota report/state show Accounting/Enforcement ON with datauser limit still 100M/100M

evidence.requirement: Post-restart proof the 100MB limit is still actively enforced by the filesystem (not just config)
evidence.summary: Live post-reboot write of 150MB stopped exactly at 100MB with 'Disk quota exceeded'; test file removed and /srv/data verified empty with quota reset to 0 used / 100M limit
